findings.title: GET /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe changes notification state
findings.body: The new endpoint is exposed as GET and TopicsController#unsubscribe immediately persists a new notification_level. Because GET requests are exempt from Rails CSRF verification and the controller skips the XHR check, any page the user visits, or a browser/link prefetch, can issue a request to /t/<id>/unsubscribe with the user's session cookies and silently change their notification state. State-changing operations should use POST/PUT or require a signed token.

findings.title: Unsubscribe crashes when no TopicUser row exists
findings.body: TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) can return nil if the user has no topic_users row for the topic (for example they have never visited it). The following conditional calls tu.notification_level, causing NoMethodError and a 500 instead of handling the unsubscribe. The code should create/update via TopicUser.change or guard against nil.

findings.title: Direct TopicUser#save bypasses notification-change bookkeeping
findings.body: The controller updates the record with tu.save! rather than TopicUser.change. TopicUser.change is the established path for notification-level changes: it sets notifications_changed_at and notifications_reason_id and publishes a MessageBus message. Bypassing it leaves stale reason/timestamp data and other browser tabs/clients will not be notified of the change.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url interpolation
findings.body: The default unsubscribe_link translation now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}. Email::MessageBuilder appends this translation whenever add_unsubscribe_link is true, but the builder does not require or default unsubscribe_url. Any current/plugin/future caller that sets add_unsubscribe_link without providing unsubscribe_url will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument while rendering the body/html, causing email send failures. It also makes the global text topic-specific.

findings.title: track_visit! assigns topic_id as user_id for integer user argument
findings.body: In track_visit!, the fallback for a non-User user argument is topic instead of user: user_id = user.is_a?(User) ? user.id : topic. Callers such as TopicsController#track_visit_to_topic pass a numeric user id, so user_id becomes the topic id. This writes topic_users rows for the wrong user (or creates rows keyed by topic_id as user_id), corrupting visit/notification tracking. It should be user_id = user.is_a?(User) ? user.id : user.

findings.title: No tests for new unsubscribe endpoint
findings.body: There are no controller/request specs for the new unsubscribe action. The PR changes state, adds redirects, and depends on TopicUser presence, but tests do not cover successful level changes, missing TopicUser, slug redirects, HTML vs JSON, or the unsafe GET behavior.
